title: Abdominal Pain Differential Diagnosis
description: Differential diagnosis for acute abdominal pain in adults, covering gastrointestinal, hepatobiliary, urologic, vascular, and gynecologic etiologies presenting to emergency or primary care settings.
source_description: Acute Abdomen in the Modern Era. Rogers SO Jr, Kirton OC. N Engl J Med 2024;391(1):60-67.

diagnoses.name: Acute Appendicitis
key_features: Periumbilical pain migrating to right lower quadrant
Rebound tenderness and guarding at McBurney point
Positive Rovsing, psoas, and obturator signs
recommended_tests: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast
Abdominal ultrasound (first-line in pregnancy and young women)

diagnoses.name: Acute Cholecystitis
key_features: Right upper quadrant or epigastric pain
Pain radiating to right shoulder or scapula
Postprandial exacerbation especially after fatty meals
red_flags: Charcot triad (fever, jaundice, RUQ pain) indicating cholangitis
Reynolds pentad (Charcot triad plus hypotension and altered mental status)
recommended_tests: Hepatobiliary markers (AST, ALT, bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase)

diagnoses.name: Acute Pancreatitis
key_features: Pain worse when supine, improved leaning forward
Lipase elevated greater than 3 times upper limit of normal
History of gallstones or alcohol use
red_flags: Grey Turner or Cullen sign indicating hemorrhagic pancreatitis
recommended_tests: CT abdomen with IV contrast (if diagnosis uncertain or no improvement at 48-72 hours)

diagnoses.name: Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm (AAA) Rupture
key_features: Sudden severe abdominal or back pain
Pain radiating to flank or groin
red_flags: Syncope with abdominal pain in elderly
recommended_tests: CT angiography of abdomen (if hemodynamically stable)
Type and crossmatch, CBC, coagulation studies

diagnoses.name: Mesenteric Ischemia
key_features: Severe abdominal pain out of proportion to physical examination
History of atrial fibrillation, atherosclerotic disease, or hypercoagulable state
Rapid onset of diffuse abdominal pain
Abdominal distension with absent bowel sounds
red_flags: Pain out of proportion to exam findings
recommended_tests: CT angiography of abdomen and pelvis

diagnoses.name: Ectopic Pregnancy
key_features: Lower abdominal or pelvic pain in reproductive-age female
red_flags: Shoulder tip pain (diaphragmatic irritation from hemoperitoneum)
recommended_tests: Serial beta-hCG if intrauterine pregnancy not confirmed

diagnoses.name: Small Bowel Obstruction
key_features: Colicky abdominal pain with intermittent cramping
red_flags: Peritoneal signs indicating bowel necrosis or perforation
recommended_tests: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast

diagnoses.name: Perforated Viscus
key_features: Sudden onset of severe diffuse abdominal pain
History of peptic ulcer disease, diverticular disease, or NSAID use
red_flags: Free air under diaphragm on imaging
recommended_tests: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast
Upright chest X-ray (free air under diaphragm)

diagnoses.name: Acute Diverticulitis
key_features: Left lower quadrant pain (most common location)
Localized tenderness without peritonitis in uncomplicated cases
recommended_tests: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast

diagnoses.name: Urolithiasis (Renal Colic)
key_features: Severe colicky flank pain radiating to groin or lower abdomen
Restlessness and inability to find comfortable position
red_flags: Fever suggesting infected obstructing stone (urological emergency)

diagnoses.name: Peptic Ulcer Disease / Gastritis
key_features: Pain improved or worsened by food intake
History of NSAID use or H. pylori infection
red_flags: Hematemesis or melena suggesting GI bleeding
recommended_tests: H. pylori testing (stool antigen or urea breath test)

diagnoses.name: Gastroenteritis
key_features: Recent sick contacts or food exposure
recommended_tests: Stool cultures if bloody diarrhea or high fever

also_consider.name: Ovarian Torsion
also_consider.rationale: Acute onset severe pelvic pain in reproductive-age women, often with nausea and vomiting; requires emergent pelvic ultrasound with Doppler

also_consider.name: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease
also_consider.rationale: Lower abdominal pain with vaginal discharge, cervical motion tenderness, and adnexal tenderness; consider in sexually active women

also_consider.name: Diabetic Ketoacidosis
also_consider.rationale: Diffuse abdominal pain may be the presenting complaint; check glucose, anion gap, and ketones in diabetic patients or new-onset diabetes

also_consider.name: Splenic Rupture or Infarction
also_consider.rationale: Left upper quadrant pain with referred left shoulder pain (Kehr sign); consider in trauma, hematologic disorders, or anticoagulation

also_consider.name: Incarcerated Hernia
also_consider.rationale: Localized pain at hernia site (inguinal, umbilical, or incisional) with irreducible mass; can progress to strangulation and bowel necrosis

also_consider.name: Testicular Torsion
also_consider.rationale: Lower abdominal pain may be referred from torsed testicle; always perform genital examination in males with lower abdominal pain

also_consider.name: Inferior Wall Myocardial Infarction
also_consider.rationale: Epigastric pain mimicking GI etiology; obtain ECG in patients with cardiovascular risk factors presenting with upper abdominal pain

also_consider.name: Adrenal Crisis
also_consider.rationale: Diffuse abdominal pain with hypotension and shock in patients on chronic corticosteroids who abruptly discontinue or under physiologic stress

also_consider.name: Herpes Zoster (Abdominal Dermatome)
also_consider.rationale: Dermatomal abdominal pain may precede vesicular rash by days; consider if pain follows a unilateral band-like distribution

also_consider.name: Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis
also_consider.rationale: Diffuse abdominal pain and fever in patients with ascites/cirrhosis; perform diagnostic paracentesis

also_consider.name: Acute Intermittent Porphyria
also_consider.rationale: Recurrent episodes of severe abdominal pain with neuropsychiatric symptoms; consider in young women with unexplained recurrent abdominal pain

also_consider.name: Familial Mediterranean Fever
also_consider.rationale: Recurrent episodes of fever and peritonitis in patients of Mediterranean descent; episodes self-resolve within 24-72 hours

clinical_reasoning_prompt: This is an evidence-based reference set, not an exhaustive differential. Abdominal pain has over 150 possible etiologies. Always assess hemodynamic stability first and rule out life-threatening causes (ruptured AAA, mesenteric ischemia, ectopic pregnancy, perforated viscus) before considering benign diagnoses. Obtain a pregnancy test in all premenopausal women. Consider extra-abdominal causes (inferior MI, pneumonia, DKA) especially in older adults. Pain location, onset pattern, and associated symptoms should guide the diagnostic workup.
